summary: Submitting a Windows name edit closes the input and shows the raw spelling until the save settles. On failure, the row shows its accepted name and the board offers Retry change and Dismiss. InlineEdit retains the failed spelling separately from the next editor. The runner verified packet 10, including its inherited Windows and Android journeys.
evidence: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture: all three cases passed in graphical Windows sessions. Each checkpoint required a fresh rustday_test read of both item IDs (42 then 17), titles and revisions before the next action.

parent_failure_retry_dismiss_and_commit: blurring three spaces from the second input to the sibling closed the editor, restored Review and showed the board-level failure and both actions. A fresh editor opened from Review. Canceling a changed draft and blurring an unchanged editor each left the failed spaces intact at one submission. Retry rejected the spaces again; Dismiss cleared the failure at two submissions. Both rows remained Review/1.

A fixture-only constraint rejected the third submission, ' Coral '. After removing the constraint and locking row 17, Retry showed exactly ' Coral ' with Saving… and no failure actions, while the row model and independent store read still showed Review. Releasing the lock committed Coral/2 on submission four. The sibling remained Review/1.

Focus comparison: a focused Windows probe first observed the sibling's display focused after the rejected blank retry, after Dismiss, during the locked retry and after commit. The full suite then asserted that destination at all four checkpoints. Sibling blur preserved focus in the reference too. When Enter or a recovery action removed its control, the reference let focus fall to the document body; Windows returned Enter to the edited display and kept the sibling focused through pointer recovery in this journey.

rejected_edit_then_save_close_and_reopen: blank Enter returned focus to the second display. Blurring a fresh correction superseded the failure, showed raw ' Review artwork ' while locked, and committed Review artwork/2. A second process displayed the accepted rows in order. display_edit_cancel_blur_and_enter passed its cancel, unchanged, blur, normalized repeat and changed Enter checkpoints.

Operator comparison: the isolated reference board, name cell and parent actions exercised the real save operation on disposable data. With the same transient constraint the reference made four save requests and two retry detail reads. Raw projections, accepted values, failure retention, dismissal and ordinary correction agreed. Full browser and network delivery were outside that comparison.

Lifetime and overlap: reconstructing the reference parent from actor/board-scoped local storage restored the failure without replay. Windows retains it only in the live view. A changed submission supersedes the failure for that name; other rows have separate state. Windows allows one pending request per row; Save re-reads the scoped name on retry and store::rename_item_if_current checks the expected title under lock. Overlapping same-field requests, simultaneous sibling failures and multi-writer window parity remain open.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed all eight portable integration cases, including commit failure and conflict recovery in desktop_edit. cargo build --locked --workspace --bins, both workspace and Android formatting checks, and workspace Clippy with native-smoke and warnings denied passed.

The first runner stopped when the dedicated emulator exited before the Android frame gate. After restarting that AVD, the ordinary runner completed: offline Kit frame and second-row touch, all 13 Node regressions, same-board delivery, all three named Windows cases, portable workspace tests, formatting and workspace binary build. Runner status: 10-windows-name-recovery verified.

08 regression: Android rejected the empty name, preserved the correction on IME Back and committed Coral on Save. The same activity (PID 3877) resumed with unsaved Amber. On the same fixture board, the Windows window displayed Review sketch (42) above Coral (17), with neither editor mounted. Cold Android reopen in PID 4529 displayed both accepted names; fresh reads confirmed revisions 1 and 2.
